draft.title: Multiplying and dividing decimals
card: To multiply decimals, ignore the decimal points and multiply as whole numbers. For \(0.3 \times 0.4\), work out \(3 \times 4 = 12\).
Count the decimal places in both numbers together. Put that many places in the answer. Here the count is \(1 + 1 = 2\), so \(0.3 \times 0.4 = 0.12\).
To divide by a decimal, move the point the same number of places to the right in both numbers, until the number you divide by is whole. Then divide.
For \(1.5 \div 0.3\), move the point one place in both. It becomes \(15 \div 3 = 5\).
draft.remember: Multiplying: count the places. Dividing: move the point the same way in both numbers.

a.why: \(6 \times 7 = 42\). The count of places is \(1 + 2 = 3\), so the answer is \(0.042\). Using only 2 places gives \(0.42\), which forgets to count the place in \(0.6\).
a.clue: Count the places in both numbers together.

b.q: Mia pours 4.8 litres of juice into cups that each hold 0.4 litres. How many cups does she fill?
b.why: Move the point one place in both numbers: \(4.8 \div 0.4\) becomes \(48 \div 4 = 12\). Moving the point in only one number would change the answer, which is how \(1.2\) or \(120\) can appear.
b.clue: Make 0.4 a whole number, and do the same to 4.8.
